chapter: Return to Atlanta and move north
title: Meeting Buddy Bradley at the Hippodrome and learning the Tack Annie
summary: At a Philadelphia charity show Green meets Bradley, who teaches him a heel-click step with the Tack Annie and tells them to find him at the Benepeer studio in New York.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: She says, he was going to be in Philadelphia pretty soon, and she was going to take us to see him. He was going to be at the Hippodrome Theater. They was having, I think, a charity show. And these important schools, they was going to have some choir, boys' choir from Notre Dame or some important school, was going to sing, and Paul Whiteman's band, you know.

And, well, the show lasted about three hours and a half, you know, and different churches and things, and Mr. Bradley was going to be there appearing in the show that was already at the theater. And that's what she did. She taken us to see the show, and she took us backstage, you know. She got us, she really put us in the show. She got us in the show, you know. We were supposed to dance.

And after we saw -- like the show -- we saw Mr. Buddy Bradley. He was doing a scene, some kind of satire about the (inaudible). (Laughter) He was a great person, you know, and very lovable. Everybody loved him. He was admired by all, you see. And that's the first time anyone taught me anything
about dancing besides my Aunt Edna B. Saunders and Chuckles, you see. I'd say Slim, because that was what he was then, Slim. We was Shorty and Slim then, you know.

He -- we were backstage. I was asking Chuckles a question. I was asking Slim a question about how should I do that step or which --which number were we going to do first, see. We used to dance by "Sweet Sue" and "Broadway Melody." And if we had to do an encore, we would do the "Bugle Call Rag," because Slim, he liked the way I danced that, you know, because he had taught me a few of the steps in the "Bugle Call Rag," how you're supposed to do it.

And so while I was asking him this question, Mr. Buddy Bradley happened to come by, and he says, he explained to me how you do a step, a certain step and some kind of tap strut, you know. And he had the Tack Annie in it, what they call Tack Annie.

And he taught me this step. By the way, Mr. Peg Leg Bass was in this show too. He was there. So it was just a fortune, you know. I think it was a blessing to meet all these great people, you see. And he says who he was and so on and so forth. And I says, "Oh, you're the man in the picture," you know. And he laughed. He liked children, see, Mr. Bradley, Buddy Bradley.
So -- and he said, "Yes." He laughed, and he says, now, he says, "I'm going to show you something." He said, "Don't

feel bad, he said, 'you may like it. You know, if you like it, well, you can learn it, you know. So I say, 'yes, sir.' So he says, 'All right, this is the way you do it, you see.' And he showed me how to click my heels, jump up, you know, hop up, click the heels, come down and then do the Tack Annie, see. That's with the pictures, the gestures of the step, see.

And I didn't know -- people backstage, you know, I didn't know show folk applauded, you know, and, well, I finally got the step and was doing it, you know, and laughed, you know. See, I was still a child, you know, and grown people they liked children at that time. I suppose --
Please excuse me -- he seemed like such a great big man, but he was only about 21 at this time.
Yeah, he was a young man.

Yeah, right, yeah. So then I tried to show this step to Chuckles, you see. I says, now, J. D. -- Slim, see -- and we was having fun with it, and we was telling him about what a nice man Mr. Buddy Bradley was, you know, and he told us where he would be over in New York City, said he would be at the Benepeer Studios down on 46th Street.

And that's the first time I knew that streets had names after numbers, you know, like 46th Street, you know, like between Broadway and Eighth Avenue, you know, and, well, I was fascinated by it. I wanted to go to New York City.
